presentation.summary: A deliberately low, owner-only 20 centimeter countermovement-jump floor that can identify a clear development case without converting age- and sex-stratified descriptive norms into athlete truth.

authority_basis.numeric_value_explanation: The 20 centimeter value is an AGAS engineering prior. It is not extracted from the Payne study, the ACSM reference table, or a validated minimum-useful-competency analysis.
authority_basis.operational_use_explanation: A planning reviewer may provisionally adopt the value only for the owner-alpha athlete and the exact governed countermovement-jump-height estimate. The published reference remains descriptive context, not operational authority for the threshold.

governs: One owner-alpha comparison between a current estimate from the exact governed countermovement-jump protocol and a provisional 20 centimeter floor.
A below-floor result may support an explosive-power development need while retaining the estimate, observation, floor, evidence, and judgment-authority identities.
does_not_establish: A population norm, sex category, percentile, medical threshold, injury-risk threshold, or safe-jumping clearance.
That 20 centimeters is a scientific minimum, an ACSM recommendation, or an optimal target for this athlete.
An exercise selection, number of jump contacts, weekly frequency, progression rule, or permission to train.
That meeting this floor eliminates the value of explosive-power maintenance or later personal calibration.
unresolved_limitations: No reviewed scientific source validates 20 centimeters as a minimum useful competency for the owner-alpha athlete.
The Canadian reference sample is historical, age- and sex-stratified, and not established as comparable to a recreationally trained construction worker.
Wall marking, arm swing, countermovement depth, effort, familiarization, footwear, and surface may materially change the estimate.
The threshold should be replaced or withdrawn after repeatable personal baseline and response observations exist.

evidence.title: Payne et al. (2000), Canadian musculoskeletal fitness norms
evidence.population: 312 female and 259 male Canadian participants aged 15 to 69 years.
evidence.finding: The study produced age- and sex-stratified descriptive reference values for vertical jump and four other musculoskeletal fitness measures.
limitations: The study does not validate 20 centimeters as an AGAS floor.
Descriptive categories are not minimum useful competencies or safety thresholds.
The sample's applicability to the owner-alpha athlete is low.
evidence.conflict_disclosure: The PubMed record does not display a conflict-of-interest statement.

source.title: Canadian musculoskeletal fitness norms
provenance_notes: Title, authors, journal, DOI, sample size, age range, and tested measures were checked against the PubMed record.
The abstract is intentionally not copied into the stored snapshot.
This release uses the paper to identify the provenance and population of the descriptive norms, not to create an AGAS competency floor.

claim.claim: Payne and colleagues produced age- and sex-stratified Canadian musculoskeletal fitness norms, including vertical jump, from 571 participants aged 15 to 69 years; these descriptive data do not validate a universal or owner-specific minimum competency.
claim.population: 312 female and 259 male Canadian participants aged 15 to 69 years.
claim.intervention: Musculoskeletal fitness testing that included vertical jump and four other measures.
claim.comparator: Age- and sex-stratified descriptive reference distributions.
claim.outcome: Population reference values for the included musculoskeletal fitness measures.
claim.effect_direction: Not applicable; this is descriptive reference information.
claim.uncertainty: A Canadian sample collected more than two decades ago may not represent the current athlete, recreationally trained adults, or occupationally active adults.
limitations: The PubMed abstract does not establish a sport- or occupation-specific competency threshold.
Age and sex categories describe a reference distribution rather than a required level for safe or effective training.
This release does not infer sex or apply a normative category to the athlete.
claim.applicability_notes: The age range includes mid-thirties adults, but the sample is not established as a match for a recreationally trained construction worker.
claim.reviewer: Codex floor-support evidence synthesis candidate; authority pending

evidence_review_content.source_verification_rationale: The title, authors, identifiers, sample size, sex counts, age range, tested measures, and normative purpose were checked against PMID 11098155.
evidence_review_content.extraction_rationale: The claim records only the descriptive reference population and explicitly excludes conversion of its categories into an AGAS floor.
evidence_review_content.evidence_strength_rationale: Low reflects one cross-sectional normative sample rather than a validated minimum for this athlete's goals or training decisions.
evidence_review_content.applicability_rationale: Low avoids treating a broad historic Canadian reference sample as equivalent to a mid-thirties recreationally trained, physically working adult.
evidence_review_content.uncertainty: Sampling, cohort, sex classification, and measurement context limit transfer.
evidence_review_content.conflict_disclosure: The PubMed record does not display a conflict-of-interest statement.

authority.statement: For the owner-alpha athlete only, treat 20.0 centimeters under the exact governed countermovement-jump protocol as a provisional minimum useful repeat-performance floor.
authority.population: Owner-only alpha; age 30 to 39; recreationally trained adult doing physical work.
authority.rationale: Twenty centimeters is a deliberately low sentinel intended to distinguish a clearly limited result from one that should not automatically receive deficit-only development under this provisional rule. It does not encode a sex category or scientific optimum.
authority.applicability_notes: Use only with a current estimate from the exact governed countermovement-jump protocol after its separate readiness and recent-exposure gates are satisfied. Review after repeat personal measurements exist.
authority.uncertainty: No scientific source validates 20 centimeters as a minimum useful athletic competency, and a first personal result cannot establish whether this threshold is appropriately calibrated.
limitations: This threshold has no population-validity claim.
It cannot establish medical safety, tissue readiness, injury risk, or an exercise dose.
Meeting it does not show that explosive power is optimal or should be ignored.
Personal longitudinal calibration should replace it when enough observations exist.
authority.authored_by: AGAS engineering candidate prepared by Codex
authority.qualification_context: System engineering synthesis; not user-authored and not a claim of a licensed clinical or strength credential. A planning reviewer must explicitly adopt the exact judgment before operational use.

authority_review_content.attestation: I adopt this exact owner-alpha product judgment for narrow planning use and understand that 20 centimeters is not a scientific finding, population norm, safety clearance, or exercise prescription.
authority_review_content.uncertainty: Approval does not establish external validity; replace or withdraw this authority when personal calibration or better applicable evidence supports a different decision.

floor.population: Owner-only alpha; age 30 to 39; exact governed countermovement-jump protocol.
floor.applicability_notes: Compare only with a current estimate from the matching governed protocol. Use the result as one planning input; never as diagnosis, safety clearance, or a universal explosive-power judgment.
floor.uncertainty: The threshold is an explicit AGAS engineering judgment with descriptive reference context but no numeric scientific validation. It is provisional and replaceable after personal calibration.

floor_review_content.applicability_rationale: Approve only for the owner-alpha athlete, ages 30 to 39, after a current estimate from the exact governed countermovement-jump protocol. The comparison may inform development or maintenance but is not a medical or safety decision.
floor_review_content.uncertainty: The source provides descriptive context only; the number 20 does not come from it. Approval adopts the separate reviewed engineering authority and requires later personal calibration.

release.release_rationale: Provide one honest, owner-reviewable explosive-power floor so the governed countermovement-jump estimate can enter planning without inferring sex or disguising a product judgment as a normative finding.
release.release_uncertainty: Ratification would authorize only this owner-alpha comparison. It creates no diagnosis, universal norm, readiness clearance, adaptation priority, exercise selection, contact dose, session, or permission to train.
